page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-176-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processors. It delivers 176 vCPUs across 88 physical cores operating at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz, supported by 105 MB of shared L3 cache. The system is equipped with 704.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with an integrated array of 32 local NVMe SSDs totaling 12,864 GB, while hardware acceleration is omitted with zero GPUs installed.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded computational power alongside substantial memory and I/O bandwidth. In parallel workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (146,317.93) and PassMark CPU tests (105,109.55), heavily boosted by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector support. Data throughput is equally strong, delivering 445.45 GB/sec uncached large-block read memory bandwidth, 164.22 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 127.49 GB/sec in static web throughput. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1,715.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (26.4 GB/sec), sit within average percentiles, reflecting a focus on total throughput rather than extreme single-core frequencies.

By consolidating dense multi-core processing, substantial RAM, and extensive local NVMe storage onto a single virtual node, the instance delivers high qualitative efficiency for IOPS-demanding scenarios, reducing dependence on external network block storage. This profile makes it well suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory key-value stores, high-concurrency static web serving, and large-scale parallel software build pipelines.

The architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache along with advanced AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, though it excludes discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute performance and memory throughput, alongside high transaction velocity reaching 164.22 million Redis operations per second and 127.49 GB/sec static web throughput.
